messages.author: c9573d5f110a3778
messages.subject: Simultaneous simulation on Hadoop cluster
parts:
I have started running my retail store simulation on a Hadoop cluster.  Currently, I have a script set up to run the simulation hundreds of times for a store (with different inputs), then summarise the results in post-processing.  The script then moves onto the next store to evaluate (using a loop).  To speed things up I'd like to be able to run the simulation for multiple stores simultaneously, preferably from the same script.  Is there a way to do this using apply, purrr, or some other method?

Thanks
Ralph

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Simultaneous simulation on Hadoop cluster
parts:
2018-04-27 15:27 GMT+02:00 Ralph Asher <ralph....@gmail.com>:
> I have started running my retail store simulation on a Hadoop cluster.
> Currently, I have a script set up to run the simulation hundreds of times
> for a store (with different inputs), then summarise the results in
> post-processing. The script then moves onto the next store to evaluate
> (using a loop). To speed things up I'd like to be able to run the
> simulation for multiple stores simultaneously, preferably from the same
> script. Is there a way to do this using apply, purrr, or some other method?

Take a look at this vignette: https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-aa-5g

What we do there basically is to encapsulate the simulation into a
function that accepts several parameters as input. Then we define a
grid of cases, with a number of parameters, and run the simulation
with parallel::mclapply. Of course you can substitute the latter with
futures ('future' package) if you want to use other parallelisation
backends.

Iñaki

> Ralph

Ralph
